prompts.inspection: Create a realistic industrial metrology photograph, landscape 3:2 1536x1024. Macro close-up of a mechanically correct conventional OUTSIDE MICROMETER measuring the outside diameter of a short smooth precision-ground STEEL CYLINDER lying HORIZONTALLY. The steel cylinder runs diagonally back into the image, perpendicular to the micrometer's measurement axis. A rigid U-shaped forged dark-grey frame sits BELOW the cylinder, embracing it; stationary flat anvil contacts the leftmost side of the cylinder, and the MOVABLE STRAIGHT SPINDLE contacts its rightmost side at EXACTLY THE SAME HEIGHT. Anvil, spindle, straight sleeve/barrel, straight knurled thimble and small ratchet knob share ONE PERFECTLY STRAIGHT HORIZONTAL AXIS. The U frame never bends the spindle or sleeve. Show both actual contact points, opposing flat contacts touching cylindrical surface across its diameter, realistic conventional instrument proportions. Micrometer held by two gloved hands cropped at wrists, user from Thailand workshop context but no face, no text on clothing, no people in background. Clean granite inspection surface, neutral blurred workshop behind. Crisp measurement contact geometry. No impossible bent barrel, no extra stems, no digital display, no labels, no readable scale values, no logos. Educational illustrative photograph, not a certificate or documented measurement.
prompts.warpage: Realistic engineering teaching photograph, landscape 3:2 1536x1024. Side-on low-angle close-up of a single thin rectangular aluminium plate after machining, resting FREELY without clamps on a truly flat dark granite inspection surface. The plate is visibly and gently bowed upward in its centre, both end edges resting on the flat surface, a clear shallow light gap beneath the middle. Uniform plate thickness 4 mm approximately with realistic 200 mm long scale proportions; smooth continuous curvature, no folds, cracks, ripples, bent corners or surreal geometry. A machinist's precision straightedge is laid BESIDE the plate on the granite, parallel to its length as a flat reference, not on top and not clamping it. Neutral workshop background, clean close-up, no instruments pretending to report a numerical result, no hands or people, no text, arrows, labels, numbers or logos. The bow is deliberately exaggerated to make free-state distortion visible. Photographic illustration of shape only; do not imply a specific cause of distortion or measured tolerance.
prompts.chatter: Realistic macro industrial teaching photograph, landscape 3:2 1536x1024. One simple solid rectangular aluminium billet secured in a conventional milling vise, viewed closely at an exposed VERTICAL MACHINED SIDE WALL. On that wall clearly visible REPEATED WAVY CHATTER BANDS: dense, regular but slightly varying diagonal rippled scallop marks from unstable milling, a washboard-like periodic texture running across the flat wall. Adjacent top horizontal surface has fine ordinary machining lay, providing a restrained visual comparison without text or split screen. Straight coherent billet edges, no wavy silhouette: the defect is a surface texture rather than a bent part. Small authentic aluminium chips, blurred stationary end mill and CNC enclosure in background safely away from the surface. Do not show sparks, cracks, deeply gouged craters or rust. No people, no text, labels, arrows, legends, gauges or logos. Educational illustrative image, no exact roughness or diagnosis claimed.
